title: lightweight context-switch emulator and batched kvcache sampler
author: Jonah Patel
release_notes: Adds a lightweight sequence-context-switch emulator and a batched KV-cache sampler; new reporter exports quantile-resilience metrics and per-phase cache hit trajectories. Useful for multi-tenant and small-batch latency experiments.
description: Motivation: Production latency regressions at p95/p99 sometimes coincide with rapid context switches between short sequences (e.g. webhooks + chat) where the KV cache thrashes in micro-batches. We needed a lightweight runner that can emulate context-switch frequency and a sampler that reports batched KV-cache eviction/hit trajectories so we can correlate kernel scheduling with cache resilience. This PR introduces: 1) seqswitch: a compact simulator for sequence context switching and micro-batching. It can replay a hybrid workload composed of long conversational sequences and short stateless calls, injecting configurable switch intervals and coalescing patterns. 2) batched-kvcache-sampler: a probe that runs alongside workloads to sample KV cache state in batch boundaries; it produces time-series of per-key residency and eviction counts and a derived "cache resilience" curve (how quickly a key is re-primed after eviction under given concurrency). 3) quantile-resilience-reporter: a reporting pipeline that merges latency quantiles with cache-resilience traces and emits a delta report keyed by phase and kernel family. Design notes: - The emulator targets low overhead: it is implemented as a Rust microservice (bench/seqswitch) that instructs the existing workload runner to vary sequence boundaries and injection timing rather than forking full additional VM workloads. This keeps experiments reproducible and cheap. - The sampler instruments the runtime's kvcache metrics via a lightweight sampling API (bench/samplers/batched_kvcache). It performs synchronized snapshots at batch commit boundaries to avoid tainting latency numbers. - Reporting: new exporter (bench/reporters/quantile_resilience) takes: latency_histogram, kvcache_snapshots, kernel_tags and produces CSV + JSON summary with fields: phase, model, kernel_family, p50/p95/p99, median_resilience_time_ms, fraction_keys_evicted, repriming_rate_10s. Checklist: - [x] seqswitch runner implemented with config-driven phase scripts - [x] batched kvcache sampler with snapshot sync - [x] reporter CSV/JSON outputs + unit tests - [x] end-to-end integration in bench harness - [x] docs: README with example configs and interpretation guide Commits (high level): - a1d3f9a: initial seqswitch scaffold and config grammar - b7c4e92: implement burst-switch scheduling and sampling hooks - c2d9f77: add batched kvcache sampling and proto exporter - 5e8a1c0: quantile_resilience reporter and CSV schema - 9f4b2a6: glue tests and harness integration + docs Changes (high level files modified): - bench/seqswitch/src/main.rs (new) - bench/seqswitch/configs/sample_hybrid.yaml (new) - bench/samplers/batched_kvcache.rs (new) - bench/reporters/quantile_resilience.rs (new) - bench/harness/integration.rs (modified) - bench/metrics/README.md (modified) - bench/tests/seqswitch_integration.rs (new) - bench/tests/kvcache_sampler_unit.rs (new) - ci/workflows/benchmark.yml (modified: added job run for seqswitch) - tools/plots/resilience_plotter.py (new) - docs/benchmark-lab/seqswitch.md (new) Review conversation (trimmed timeline): "Maria Kovacs": "Nice focused change. Two concerns: how do we ensure snapshots don't perturb latency? and can we run this on the mini-cluster locally?" "Jonah Patel (author)": "Snapshots are taken only at batch commit boundaries using the runtime's snapshot hook; I've added a flag --sync-snapshot that enforces that. For local mini-cluster, see sample_hybrid.yaml which runs with smaller concurrency and the harness autodeploy target 'mini'." "Ellen Park": "Can the sampler be adapted to test quantized kernels where KV representation differs?" "Jonah Patel": "Yes — sampler reads runtime kernel tags and normalizes keys by (model, quantization_level) so reports are comparable. I added a unit test kvcache_sampler_unit.rs to cover a quantized pseudo-kv layout." "Samir Rao (SRE)": "CI failed on first run: test timeouts in integration harness. Re-run once fixed?" "Jonah Patel": "Fixed a race in harness startup by adding a readiness probe and increasing default timeout; re-ran CI." CI summary: - ci/unit: pass - ci/integration: pass (initial failure on 2024-09-11 due to race; subsequent run on 2024-09-12 passed) - bench-suite: pass - lint: pass How to use (short): - example config: bench/seqswitch/configs/sample_hybrid.yaml - run: ./bin/bench run --runner seqswitch --config sample_hybrid.yaml - outputs: bench/out/<run-id>/quantile_resilience.json and .csv Notes on interpreting results: - The reporter aligns per-batch kvcache snapshots with latency buckets by matching run-phase timestamps; use resilience_plotter.py to plot "repriming_rate" vs p95 to identify unstable kernels. - Typical signal: rising p95 concurrent with a drop in median_resilience_time_ms implies eviction-driven tail amplification. Backwards compatibility: - The changes are additive; existing harnesses that don't opt into seqswitch or the kvcache sampler will not be affected. Performance impact: - seqswitch adds negligible overhead when idle; sampler sampling cost is proportional to sampled-key-count (default 200 keys) and is documented in metrics/README. Tests: - Unit tests for sampler normalization and config parser added. - Integration test runs a 30s mini-run on the mini-cluster verifying CSV output and schema. Merge: Squashed and merged to main on 2024-09-18 (merge method: squash). Follow-ups: - ENG-2310: add cross-run aggregator to group resilience metrics across multiple runs for baseline regression detection. - ENG-2211: run this experiment across the dedicated cluster fleet to generate a baseline report for Q4.
